harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established a persistent AIDE integrity baseline for /etc on node1. It monitors file content, type, permissions, ownership, links, size, ACLs, SELinux labels, and extended attributes across 1,190 entries. A daily persistent timer writes the latest report to /var/log/aide/etc-integrity-report.latest. Content-change detection and clean restoration were demonstrated, and the final configuration remained healthy across reboot.
actions_performed: Created the dedicated policy /etc/aide-etc.conf and protected it with mode 0600.
Created and enabled aide-etc-check.timer for persistent daily checks.
Generated /var/lib/aide/aide-etc.db.gz and protected it with mode 0600.
Demonstrated detection of a controlled /etc/issue content change, including changed size and SHA-256.
Restored /etc/issue and confirmed a clean 1,190-entry check.
Excluded volatile inode/mtime/ctime metadata after observing normal boot-time churn, while retaining content and security-attribute checks.
Safely restarted node1 and verified changed boot identities, system recovery, timer persistence, unchanged baseline database hash, and clean post-restart checks.

evidence.summary: The final policy covers /etc with SHA-256 and security metadata checks; the database contains 1,190 entries and policy/database/report files are root-owned mode 0600.

evidence.requirement: Identify and report later file changes
evidence.summary: A controlled content modification to /etc/issue was reported with changed size and SHA-256; restoration returned the check to no differences and status 0.
The daily persistent systemd timer is enabled and scheduled, with reports written to /var/log/aide/etc-integrity-report.latest.

Captured healthy baseline at boot ID 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723, received native reboot acknowledgement, observed boot ID 5c276c31-db4d-472e-a4f2-0e6989c612d5, and verified system/timer/database recovery. Boot-time metadata churn was diagnosed and the policy refined to a clean state.

Captured a clean pre-restart baseline at boot ID 5c276c31-db4d-472e-a4f2-0e6989c612d5, received reboot acknowledgement, observed new boot ID 3a4b1704-7324-47a5-935a-4f0789509d78, and confirmed system running, timer active/enabled, AIDE installed, identical database hash, and a clean post-restart check.
